newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down across the board on Tuesday on weak market sentiment, traders said.
The most active September 1997 contract ended at 23,280 yuan ($2,807) per tonne, losing 180 yuan. It opened at 23,430 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,450 and a low of 23,260.
June fell 100 to 22,670, July 120 to 22,880, August 150 to 23,050, October 130 to 23,400 and November 110 to 23,400.
Combined volume rose to 29,310 tonnes from 18,000.
Copper opened slightly lower and fell steadily for most of the session, traders said.
Traders said many investors were pessimistic about the short term market trend and most of them were willing to sell at high levels.
"Liquidition selling plus large amounts of speculative selling emerged on the market in the morning session," one trader said. "Investors are also pessimistic about weak physical copper prices."
Physical prices are around 22,800 yuan in the Shanghai area, down from 23,000 last week, traders said.
Traders said fundamentals were not in favour of buyers with the approach of the summer low consumption season.
"Copper demand usually decreases in summer and the recent soft physical prices have reflected the trend," a second trader said.
Traders said they expected copper prices to maintain a downward trend in the short term.
Aluminium ended down, following copper's trend.
June fell 350 to 14,500, July 200 to 14,700, August 100 to 15,000 and September 150 to 15,000.
Combined volume fell to 1,180 tonnes from 1,290.
